title: RAW UNREVIEWED: one herbal entry separates remedy recipients from an animal naming epilogue
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. Complete Pseudo-Apuleius CXIII has two numbered remedy indications, habitat, and a hare-benefit narrative ending ideo leporina dicitur. A whole-entry reading preserves one herb while separating remedy recipients from the animal that motivates its name; the drawn animal need not be every prescription patient.

source.locator: Primary-edition check CXIII, CML IV1927 p198, with subsequent subponitur and apparatus corrections
source.layer: Complete critical-edition chapter and apparatus read by AL/root; this producer read their retained full transcription, not pixels

design.whole_account: Keep the same named herb through fever/pillow placement, eye-hair obstruction, habitat, and the subsequent hare naming explanation. Two prospective remedy clauses do not become one observed treatment episode. Haec herba resumes the herb; the hare is beneficiary of the distinct naming narrative; ideo consumes that narrative as rationale for leporina dicitur.
design.owned_target_relation: GDT1142 REPORT retains f25v leaf-mouth continuity and separately outlined animal body. This permits an already exposed potential animal naming vignette, not an identified plant, animal, patient or word. A later root-selected complete f25v reading must retain all its existing paragraph boundaries; no target text opened, no source-to-paragraph count equation.
linked_consequences: One herb must remain the remedy material and the object named at the end; replacing it with a new plant at the animal clause breaks source co-reference.
Assigning the animal as every remedy recipient requires an explicit additional scope bridge; the ending naming rationale does not itself supply that bridge.
A source-preserving complete composition must give the naming predicate a reason consumer, distinct from prescription efficacy and from an instruction that the reader copy animal behavior.
design.contrast: Universal pictured-patient account versus a mixed-function entry with remedy indications and an animal name explanation. Mere emblem labels omit the actual reason clause; an exemplum-to-human instruction adds a return/directive absent from this chapter.
limitations: Human recipients of the first two indications are contextual interpretation: the quoted base chapter does not print homo. Price this assumption; do not claim an independently explicit human/animal type collision.
The base text remedies the hare but does not state eating. Beta has comedit and omits aestu; never combine base heat and beta eating into one recovered witness.
No target repeated name, reason connective, recipient or whole reading is identified; all remain paid C0 possibilities.
Globally renamed referents preserve the relations and prevent unique meaning selection; this does not prohibit exploratory authorship.
design.falsifier_and_decision: For a later declared whole C0 source-preserving reading, reject loss of shared herb identity or a naming clause without its narrative operand. If its prescribed recipient changes only by silently importing picture ownership, remove that unpriced bridge rather than announce a translated patient. A complete compatible account retains this alternative without selecting semantics; source-only compatibility is not a target test.

predecessors.IDEA000810: Repeated stem-as-spindle relation across naming/description; no split prescription recipients and animal naming narrative.
predecessors.IDEA000868: Shared lexical key for name/comparator; this proposal assumes no lexical key or productive etymological morphology.
predecessors.IDEA000744: Animal consumption before danger; here two remedy indications and an animal-name epilogue, no opponent encounter.

design.stop: RAW retention only. No authoring, target query, parser, reserve or experiment selection in this five-minute task; root reviews novelty and whole-target scope separately.
design.access: Existing source reports/RAWs only; no new source/target pixels, target body, acquisition, contact, globals or Git.
